body:
Catches "works on my machine" before a release leaves the build: dependencies, files or environment variables that the build machine has but the package doesn't carry.

- A build runs from a recorded copy of the source in a separate folder, with locked dependencies, rather than on the working tree as it is (D-246 left this to this feature).
- The build records what it read from the machine: environment variables, files outside the project, tools on `PATH`. Tool versions are already recorded with each release (D-247).
- The final package is inspected: its file list, linked libraries, and expected files that are missing.
- An agent reviews the inspection and reports risks in plain language (e.g. "reads `SOLACE_CONFIG` but nothing sets it in the package"); the human sees the report with the release, and can file a task from any finding.

Later milestones: deploying and testing the release in a sandbox (Deploy and Test tabs).

Depends on: build: run from the Build page, build: artifacts and versions (both complete).
title: build: package inspection
